Inotropic agents.recommendation_when_to_consider: May be considered in patients with SBP <90 mmHg and evidence of hypoperfusion who do not respond to standard treatment, including fluid challenge, to improve peripheral perfusion and maintain end-organ function.
Inotropic agents.recommendation_when_not_routinely_used: Not recommended routinely due to safety concerns, unless the patient has symptomatic hypotension and evidence of hypoperfusion.

Vasopressors.recommendation: A vasopressor, preferably norepinephrine, may be considered in patients with cardiogenic shock to increase blood pressure and vital organ perfusion.

Thromboembolism_prophylaxis.recommendation: Thromboembolism prophylaxis (e.g., with low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH)) is recommended in patients not already anticoagulated and with no contraindication to anticoagulation to reduce the risk of deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
Thromboembolism_prophylaxis.notes: Apply unless patient is already anticoagulated or has contraindications.

Opiates.recommendation: Routine use of opiates is not recommended, unless in selected patients with severe/intractable pain or anxiety.

Digoxin (section 11.3.8).indication: Should be considered in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) with a rapid ventricular rate (>110 b.p.m.) despite beta-blockers.
Digoxin (section 11.3.8).dosing: Can be given in boluses of 0.25–0.5 mg IV if not used previously.
Digoxin (section 11.3.8).special_considerations: In patients with comorbidities (e.g., CKD) or other factors affecting digoxin metabolism, and/or the elderly, maintenance dose may be difficult to estimate; measurements of serum digoxin concentrations should be performed.
Digoxin (section 11.3.8).alternatives_and_research: Digitoxin is a potential alternative being evaluated in a randomized placebo-controlled trial (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03783429).
Digoxin (section 11.3.8).references: See cross-reference to section 12.1.1 and cited references.

Thromboembolism prophylaxis (section 11..recommendation: Thromboembolism prophylaxis with heparin (e.g., LMWH) or another anticoagulant is recommended, unless contraindicated or unnecessary because of existing oral anticoagulant treatment.
